messages:
incident-bot: P0 alert: continuous-batcher memory growth causing node flaps and CUDA allocation failures in us-west-2. Multiple containers OOM-killed and some nodes auto-drained by autoscaler. Pager -> @alice (oncall)

alice (oncall): seeing huge tail latencies in the batcher traces, plus pods in CrashLoopBackOff. markers: CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED and then cgroup OOM in kubelet logs.

ben (eng-runtime): confirmed. stack: continuous-batcher keeps growing queued batch sizes past limits when prefetch tokens spike. Observed batch_accumulator size blowing up from 4->120 in <30s. gpu memory climbs until cudaAlloc fails.

carla (eng-sre): impacted AZs: us-west-2a/b. Autoscaler drained 3 nodes so customer traffic got routed to remaining nodes -> latency cascaded. Support reports ~1.2% 5xx across region and several important customers seeing 20-60s completions.

alice (oncall): timeline? did anything deploy recently to batcher/prefetch?

ben (eng-runtime): yes, 03:10 UTC rolled a change that made prefetchtill_min_age configurable per model and changed the backpressure accounting to use queued_token_estimate instead of inflight_tokens. commit 4f7c9a2. suspect race: queued_token_estimate undercounts on eviction path -> batcher allowed unbounded enqueue.

derek (support): customer impact: a few enterprise jobs time out; one partner reported failure during demo. Escalation to CSM in progress.

elaine (eng-oncall): immediate mitigation suggestions?

ben (eng-runtime): quick fixes we can try now: 1) set environment override MAX_BATCH_ACCUM_SIZE=20 on batcher deployment 2) disable kv-prefetch for high-qps models (CONFIG_DISABLE_KV_PREFETCH=true) 3) apply emergency throttle rule for POST /v1/generate with token cap 512.

carla (eng-sre): I'm going to cordon/drain node ip-10-0-14-* to get pid state cleaned and restart kube-proxy on those nodes after pods are terminated. also triggering a rolling restart of batcher ds.

deploy-bot: deploy started: patch/batcher-emergency-limits (by carla) -> rolling restart 12/24 pods. ETA 3m per pod.

alice (oncall): applying MAX_BATCH_ACCUM_SIZE override to live config now.

ben (eng-runtime): added hotfix patch: revert queued_token_estimate usage and reapply inflight_tokens accounting. small diff:
```
- acc += queued_token_estimate(req)
+ acc += inflight_tokens(req)
```
this prevents enqueueing when inflight budget exhausted. pushing as hot-restart to avoid full redeploy.

ben (eng-runtime): also instrumented debug gauge batcher.accumulator.size to 2s TTL and pushed to console so we get immediate telemetry.

carla (eng-sre): after first pod restarts, memory growth stabilized on that instance. overall 5xx rate down from 1.2% -> 0.25% in last 6m.

derek (support): customers reporting partial recovery, still seeing occasional spikes. continuing to notify top 10 accounts.

alice (oncall): stack traces I grabbed from crashed pods:
```
E tensorflow: CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED at cublasAllocate
E runtime: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory (allocation 1.5G)
E kernel: batcher::apply_batch - reserve failed
```
and kube logs: `OOMKilled` followed by `containerd: failed to create task` on restart attempts.

ben (eng-runtime): suggests temp capacity increase: scale batcher pool +20% to absorb. I'm kicking extra nodes in us-west-2 for 10m.

carla (eng-sre): doing that now: scaled nodegroup batcher-workers +4 -> new nodes coming up.

deploy-bot: patch/batcher-emergency-limits applied successfully to 12 pods.

elaine (eng-oncall): after hotfix and limit, we're seeing batch_accumulator peak at ~18 consistently, GPU mem stable, no new OOMs in last 7m. backpressure is reasserting.

alice (oncall): will keep monitoring for 30m, then plan handback. Ben, we should still prepare a rollback of the 03:10 change and a proper patch for accounting race.

ben (eng-runtime): agreed. I'll open PR with tests that simulate eviction and enqueue races. planning: revert change in staging, add linearizable update to queue accounting, and add e2e that enforces batch size invariant.

derek (support): customer-impact summary for status page: "We experienced increased latency and errors in us-west-2 between 03:12-03:40 UTC due to internal batching issue; mitigations applied and service restored. Some requests may have timed out." Want me to include that?

carla (eng-sre): yes, but be specific: include numbers: ~1.2% error spike, ~3 nodes cycled, temporary 20-60s latency for some completions.

derek (support): noted. drafting post to status. will send to legal for review for customer-facing language.

alice (oncall): handoff: I'll stay on for 45m to verify stability. @elaine pick up next oncall at 04:15 UTC. If tail latencies reappear, escalate to incident leads and consider full rollback of 4f7c9a2.

elaine (eng-oncall): acknowledged. adding runbook steps to thread: 1) set MAX_BATCH_ACCUM_SIZE=20; 2) toggle CONFIG_DISABLE_KV_PREFETCH=true for suspect models; 3) scale pool +25% temporarily; 4) roll hotfix to revert queued_token_estimate -> inflight_tokens; 5) monitor batch_accumulator.size and gpu_mem.used gauges.

ben (eng-runtime): follow-up items (tracking): - PR with proper fix (tests) - add hard caps on accumulator in runtime - add alert when accumulator.size > 30 for >1m - add abort/reject path when inflight_budget would be exceeded.

carla (eng-sre): postmortem owner? assigning to ben + carla. support owner: derek. timeline owner: alice.

incident-bot: P0 -> downgraded to P2 at 03:44 UTC after stabilization and no new OOMs for 30m.

alice (oncall): final note: root cause appears to be accounting change + prefetch token burst pattern which exposed a race. we'll run load tests that mimic prefetch bursts and token evictions. thanks all. :thumbsup:

derek (support): posting status update now. notifying affected customers.

elaine (eng-oncall): capturing this thread into incident tracker and scheduling postmortem meeting for tomorrow 09:00 UTC.

ben (eng-runtime): adding commit refs and logs to the incident doc. commit 4f7c9a2 (prefetch accounting change) and hotfix revert 7a2d1e0.

carla (eng-sre): closing live mitigation. continuing to monitor for 2h.

# end of thread
